title: Quality control and doublet detection in a two-sample bone-marrow multiome workflow

sources.locator: cells 3-18, headings Quality Control and Doublet detection

scientific_use: Loads two filtered feature-barcode matrices from healthy-donor bone-marrow mononuclear cells, combines them with a sample label, computes gene-population QC metrics, applies permissive cell/gene filters, and runs Scrublet by sample. Outputs per-cell QC annotations and doublet_score/predicted_doublet; supports deciding which cells to retain before downstream analysis.
tool_role_basis: Applies documented Scanpy read, QC, filter, and Scrublet APIs to study data; no implementation of these algorithms is shown.

inputs.meaning: Two 10x HDF5 filtered feature-barcode matrices (s1d1 and s1d3) and prefixes defining mitochondrial, ribosomal, and hemoglobin genes; concatenated AnnData with sample labels.
inputs.format: 10x Genomics HDF5 converted to AnnData; gene sets marked in .var; sample in .obs['sample'].
inputs.stage: Filtered matrices are already provided; no raw read processing is shown.

outputs.meaning: QC metrics including gene/cell counts, total counts and proportions for gene subsets; filtered observations/features; Scrublet scores and predicted doublet labels.
outputs.format: AnnData .obs/.var annotations and filtered matrix; tutorial does not save a result artifact.

dependencies: Scanpy, AnnData, pooch, and Scrublet dependency used by scanpy.pp.scrublet.
Source data retrieval from the pinned DOI registry; sample-wise processing through batch_key='sample'.
evidence: Tutorial cells 3-5 identify source, assay, sample IDs, HDF5 input, and concatenation.
Cells 8-18 describe QC metrics, filtering rationale, Scrublet operation and result columns.
limitations: Tutorial says ~8,000 cells per sample and 36,601 measured genes; exact retained counts depend on downloaded source/version and are not execution-verified here.
The filters are permissive examples, not validated universal QC thresholds; text recommends per-sample QC for multi-batch data.
No cell-by-cell truth labels for doublet grading are identified.

title: Normalize, select variable genes, reduce dimensions, embed, and cluster bone-marrow cells

sources.locator: cells 21-41, headings Normalization, Feature selection, Dimensionality Reduction, Nearest neighbor graph construction and visualization, Clustering

scientific_use: Performs median-depth normalization and log1p, batch-aware highly-variable gene selection, PCA, neighborhood graph construction, UMAP and Leiden community detection on the combined two-sample bone-marrow expression matrix. Produces lower-dimensional coordinates and cell communities for exploratory identification of cellular structure.
tool_role_basis: Composes existing Scanpy preprocessing and analysis methods; no new algorithm implementation is shown.

inputs.meaning: AnnData from the same two samples after the tutorial's QC/filtering stage; sample labels retained for batch-aware HVG calculation.
inputs.format: Cell-by-gene count matrix in AnnData; batch key .obs['sample'].
inputs.stage: QC-filtered counts; tutorial does not preserve a raw-count layer before normalization.

outputs.meaning: Log-normalized matrix, gene-level highly_variable metrics/selection, PCA coordinates, neighbor distances/connectivities, UMAP coordinates, and Leiden cluster labels.

dependencies: Scanpy and AnnData.
Leiden graph-clustering backend; tutorial chooses flavor='igraph' and n_iterations=2.
The previous unit's QC and doublet outputs are the upstream source state; tutorial does not remove predicted doublets before this section.
evidence: Tutorial cells 21-41 specify median total-count normalization, log1p, n_top_genes=2000 with batch_key='sample', PCA, neighbors, UMAP and Leiden.
docs/api/preprocessing.md enumerates normalization, highly-variable genes and PCA as preprocessing APIs.
docs/api/tools.md classifies Leiden/UMAP as tools that add interpretable annotations.
limitations: Tutorial calls cluster resolution arbitrary and recommends biological interpretation; it gives no fixed expected cluster count.
UMAP is a visualization; no quantitative embedding accuracy criterion is specified.
No result artifact is saved by the tutorial.

dependencies: Scanpy, AnnData, Matplotlib plotting stack.
Biological interpretation from the tutorial's marker list and external curated annotation knowledge.
Upstream Leiden clustering and gene expression from scanpy-clustering-neurips21-preprocessing-clustering.

limitations: The broad labels are manual and the marker list is adapted from another resource; no independent truth labels or grading reference is supplied.

title: Reconstruct hematopoietic progenitor branches with PAGA and diffusion pseudotime

sources.locator: cells 0-63, sections Preprocessing and Visualization, Optional: Denoising the graph, Clustering and PAGA, Recomputing the embedding using PAGA-initialization, Reconstructing gene changes along PAGA paths

scientific_use: Applies the Zheng17 preprocessing recipe, PCA and a 4-neighbor graph to mouse myeloid progenitor expression data; clusters and abstracts cell-state connectivity with PAGA, lays out cells from PAGA initialization, and computes DPT relative to a chosen annotated stem cell to inspect erythroid, neutrophil and monocyte lineage paths and selected gene changes.
tool_role_basis: Uses Scanpy preprocessing, graph, Louvain, PAGA, embedding and DPT tools on supplied study data; PAGA/DPT implementation is not created in the tutorial.

inputs.meaning: Scanpy paul15 AnnData, non-logarithmized expression from hematopoietic progenitors with cluster/cell-type annotations and a root-cell index; graph derived from PCA or diffusion-map representation.
inputs.format: HDF5 source loaded to AnnData; .X expression, .obs['paul15_clusters'], .uns['iroot'].
inputs.stage: The tutorial runs recipe_zheng17, PCA, neighbors, optional diffusion map neighbor recalculation, Louvain, then PAGA. It chooses the first '16/Stem' cell as iroot before DPT. Diffusion-map coordinates must precede DPT; optional graph denoising is explicitly not required.

outputs.meaning: Cluster labels, abstracted PAGA graph and coordinates, DPT pseudotime, PAGA comparisons, and gene-expression trends for three annotated paths.
outputs.format: AnnData .obs, .uns['paga'], .obsm graph/embedding coordinates; CSV data returned by paga_path (paga_path_erythrocytes.csv, paga_path_neutrophils.csv, paga_path_monocytes.csv) and PDF plot.

dependencies: Scanpy, AnnData, graph/dimensionality-reduction dependencies and plotting stack.
The tutorial changes precision to float64 for platform consistency; older Louvain is retained to reproduce the paper workflow, with note that current practice would use Leiden.
Dataset root cell is chosen based on annotation; biological interpretation depends on the annotation and path definitions.
evidence: Tutorial cells 2-5 state the Paul et al. myeloid/erythroid differentiation use and call datasets.paul15.
Cells 9-27 show recipe, PCA, neighbors, optional diffusion denoising, Louvain and PAGA; cell 23 says Louvain is used for paper reproduction.
Cells 49-63 choose annotated stem-cell root, compute DPT, define erythroid/neutrophil/monocyte paths and marker genes, and save CSV trend tables and a PDF.

Path definitions are manually specified tutorial choices; plots and fixed cell root are not a validated lineage ground truth.

No reference run or task-level grader was executed.

title: Select variable genes and cluster two PBMC datasets using analytic Pearson residuals

sources.locator: cells 0-51, especially quality control, HVG residual selection, residual transform and downstream PCA/t-SNE/Leiden sections

scientific_use: Compares experimental analytic-Pearson-residual HVG selection and preprocessing on 10x PBMC 3k v1 and PBMC 10k v3. It compares selected genes with prior marker genes, subsets to 2,000 HVGs, transforms raw counts to residuals, then runs PCA, t-SNE, neighbors and Leiden on both datasets.
tool_role_basis: Applies experimental Scanpy Pearson-residual preprocessing wrappers and established PCA/neighbor/Leiden APIs to two 10x datasets; implementation is not changed.

inputs.meaning: Two raw UMI count matrices for PBMC 3k v1 and PBMC 10k v3, plus a small marker-gene reference set adapted from the legacy PBMC3k tutorial.
inputs.format: 10x MTX directories loaded as AnnData; sparse counts in .X, mitochondrial genes flagged in .var.
inputs.stage: Filters cells/genes and dataset-specific outliers before computing residual HVGs. The tutorial's PBMC3k thresholds are pct_counts_mt>5, total_counts>5000, n_genes_by_counts>2500; PBMC10k uses >20, >25000, >6000 respectively. Raw counts are copied to a layer before residuals densify X.

outputs.meaning: Per-gene residual variance/HVG flags and reduced expression matrix; Pearson residual representation, PCA/t-SNE, neighbor graph and Leiden cluster labels for both datasets.
outputs.format: AnnData .var and .X, .layers['raw']/['sqrt_norm'], .obsm coordinates, .obsp neighbor graph, .obs Leiden labels; marker overlays on t-SNE.

dependencies: Scanpy experimental.pp Pearson-residual functions, AnnData, 10x reader, PCA/t-SNE/neighbor and igraph Leiden dependencies.
For memory efficiency, select genes before computing residual matrix; residual transform is dense. Tutorial recommends chunksize reduction for constrained RAM.
Negative-binomial overdispersion theta defaults to 100 per tutorial discussion; clipping defaults to plus/minus sqrt(number of cells).
evidence: Notebook cells 4-8 identify two 10x chemistries/datasets and prior marker genes.
Cells 10-30 define filtering, QC thresholds and experimental.pp.highly_variable_genes(flavor='pearson_residuals', n_top_genes=2000), then subset to selected genes.
Cells 34-47 explain raw count retention, residual transform, downstream PCA/t-SNE/neighbors/Leiden and marker-gene visualization.
Cells 48-50 describe theta/clipping/chunksize constraints and full-workflow wrappers.
limitations: Notebook labels this API experimental and warns that dense residual matrices need memory; it recommends gene selection before transformation.
The exact v3 download URL suffix and current dataset metadata/terms were not independently resolved.
Tutorial's statement that selected markers are all retained is a documented claim; execution/marker recall was not validated here.
